chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Khalid al-Talisi, from Saif ibn 'Amirah, from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about those who hire out beasts of burden, who travel every day; is there shortening of prayer for them if they are on a journey? He said, 'Yes.'
ai.seo_question: Do travelers who hire animals and travel daily have to shorten their prayers?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that daily travel by hired beasts of burden qualifies one as a traveler, thereby entitling them to shorten prayers (qasr). This ruling highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical reality of movement and fatigue rather than fixed duration, distinguishing it from those who remain stationary. It underscores the practical flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding the definition of 'safar' for worship obligations.
